chunks: What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:

If you enter the place of relieving oneself and relieve yourself, then do not pour water, and then perform wudu (ablution), and forget to perform istinja', then remember after you have prayed, then re-performance is upon you. But if you had poured water, then forgot to wash your penis until you prayed, then re-performance of the wudu (ablution) and the salat (prayer), and washing of your penis, are upon you, because urine is like feces.
And it indicates that water is indispensable in the case of urine.

key_terms.الْإِعَادَةُ: repetition or re-performance of the act
key_terms.الْغَائِطَ: the place of relieving oneself; used here for going to defecate
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat (prayer)
key_terms.تَسْتَنْجِيَ: to cleanse oneself after relieving oneself

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets to wash after urinating or relieving himself before performing wudu (ablution) and salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about taharah (ritual purity) after relieving oneself and its effect on the validity of wudu (ablution) and salat (prayer). It indicates that washing with water is necessary in the case of urine, and that neglecting istinja' affects the need to repeat worship.
